questions.stem: How many addresses appear in an informal letter?

options.text: One — the writer's address only
Two — the writer's and the recipient's
None at all
Two, but both belong to the writer

questions.explanation: An informal letter goes to someone who already knows you, so only your own address is needed, and it appears at the top right with the date beneath it. Including the recipient's address is a format error that marks the letter as formal.

distractorRationale.b: Two addresses is the formal letter format
distractorRationale.c: The writer's address is still required so that a reply can be sent
distractorRationale.d: There is never any reason to write your address twice

questions.stem: Which subscription is appropriate for a letter to your mother?

options.text: Yours faithfully
Your loving son
Yours sincerely
I remain your humble servant

questions.explanation: Letters to close family use warm subscriptions such as *Your loving son*, *Your loving daughter*, *Yours affectionately* or simply *Love*. The relationship, not a fixed rule, decides the wording.

distractorRationale.a: *Yours faithfully* belongs to formal letters addressed to an unnamed official
distractorRationale.c: *Yours sincerely* is formal, used when you name an official recipient
distractorRationale.d: An archaic official formula that would sound absurd in a letter to a parent

questions.stem: Which feature belongs to a formal letter but NOT to an informal letter?

options.text: The writer's address
The date
An underlined heading stating the subject
A closing paragraph

questions.explanation: The subject heading exists so that an official can classify and route a letter, which is meaningless in a letter to a friend. An informal letter therefore moves straight from the salutation into the first paragraph.

distractorRationale.a: Both kinds of letter carry the writer's address
distractorRationale.b: Both kinds of letter carry the date
distractorRationale.d: Every letter should round off with a closing paragraph

questions.stem: Which sequence gives the correct order of the features of an informal letter?

options.text: Writer's address, date, salutation, body, subscription, name
Salutation, writer's address, date, body, subscription, name
Writer's address, recipient's address, date, salutation, heading, body, name
Date, salutation, writer's address, heading, body, subscription

questions.explanation: An informal letter has six features in a fixed order: your address, the date, the greeting, the message, the warm close and your first name. There is no recipient's address and no heading.

distractorRationale.b: Places the greeting before the address, which is never done
distractorRationale.c: Adds a recipient's address and a heading, both of which are formal features
distractorRationale.d: Separates the date from the address and inserts a heading

questions.stem: Which opening paragraph best suits a letter to a friend you have not written to for a term?

options.text: I write to inform you that I am in receipt of your correspondence dated 3 May.
How have you been? I am sorry I have kept quiet for so long — the second term nearly finished me, and I have plenty to tell you.
Reference is made to our last discussion on the aforementioned subject matter.
This letter serves to acquaint you with recent developments in my academic career.

questions.explanation: An informal letter opens with warmth: a greeting, a personal enquiry, and a natural reason for writing. Contractions and conversational phrasing are welcome here, because the register should sound like you talking to your friend.

distractorRationale.a: Official acknowledgement language that would sound cold and strange to a friend
distractorRationale.c: *Aforementioned* and *reference is made* belong to bureaucratic correspondence
distractorRationale.d: Stiff and impersonal; nobody speaks to a friend in this register

questions.stem: Because an informal letter is friendly in tone, grammatical errors and slang are not penalised in it.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. An informal register permits contractions, direct questions and a conversational rhythm, but the letter must still be written in correct Standard English. Pidgin, text-message spelling and faulty grammar are penalised in every essay task, whatever its register.

questions.stem: Which salutation is appropriate for an informal letter to your uncle?

options.text: Dear Sir
Dear Uncle Emeka
To Whom It May Concern
Dear Mr Emeka Obi

questions.explanation: An informal salutation names the person in the way you actually address them, so *Dear Uncle Emeka* is right. Using a formal salutation to a relative breaks the register and signals that the candidate has not identified the letter type.

distractorRationale.a: *Dear Sir* is for an unnamed official and would sound cold to a relative
distractorRationale.c: A formula for public notices, not for any personal letter
distractorRationale.d: Correct for a business contact, but too distant for an uncle

questions.stem: A candidate writes to a cousin: "I wish to state categorically that the aforementioned excursion was highly beneficial to my person." What is wrong with the sentence?

options.text: The grammar is faulty and the tenses do not agree
The register is too formal and stilted for a letter to a relative
It contains a contraction that is not allowed in letters
It is too short to count as a paragraph

questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically sound but written in official language — *wish to state categorically*, *aforementioned*, *to my person* — that no one would use with a cousin. Register marks are lost when the tone does not match the reader. A natural version would be: "The excursion was wonderful, and I learnt a lot."

distractorRationale.a: There is no grammatical or tense error in the sentence
distractorRationale.c: The sentence contains no contraction at all
distractorRationale.d: Length is not the problem; the choice of language is

questions.stem: Which closing paragraph best suits an informal letter to a friend?

options.text: I look forward to your favourable response on the aforementioned matter.
Do greet your parents for me, and please write back soon — I really want to hear how the trials went.
Thank you for your anticipated cooperation in this regard.
Kindly treat this letter as urgent and acknowledge receipt.

questions.explanation: An informal close sends greetings to shared acquaintances, invites a reply and keeps the warm conversational tone of the rest of the letter. The other three options are lifted from official correspondence and clash with the relationship.

distractorRationale.a: Business language; *aforementioned matter* is not how friends speak
distractorRationale.c: A stock formula from official letters requesting action
distractorRationale.d: Reads like an office memorandum demanding acknowledgement

questions.stem: A candidate's informal letter to a friend includes the friend's address on the left, an underlined heading, and the close "Yours faithfully". How many format faults are there?

options.text: One
Two
Three
None

questions.explanation: All three items are formal features wrongly imported into an informal letter: the recipient's address, the subject heading and the formal subscription. An informal letter needs only the writer's address, the date, a personal salutation, the body, a warm close and the writer's first name.

distractorRationale.a: Identifies only one of the three imported features
distractorRationale.b: Misses one of the three, most often the recipient's address
distractorRationale.d: Each of the three items breaks the informal format
